label: A holder of another that could not lack the act by which it holds cannot be lacking
paraphrase: Conclusion: it is impossible that there be no f, x and r with f distinct from x, f presently actualizing x in r, f in act in r, and f unable to lack its act in r. It says nothing of f's other respects: f may be in potency, or held, in another respect (Control part 6), so it is not the pure-act conclusion.
